cells.tense: You are standing here under real weight, and the thing you aimed at is finally paying off.
cells.act: step back far enough to see the whole arrangement
cells.ask: Take a wider view of everything you've built here, not tonight's piece. Say the shape of it to yourself in a few words, then leave it as it stands.
cells.core:
There's a pull toward something real in you, and it isn't daydreaming. It's the thing you've been pointed at, and here you've started showing it without having to announce it. What gets lit up isn't the wish — it's the work underneath the wish. You can carry weight and keep the direction at the same time, which is rarer than either one alone.

What's worth doing with that is taking a wider view while the whole thing still holds this shape. There's a pattern in what you've been building that only shows up from a little distance — the way all of it hooks to the same thing. Step back. Put words to it. Then leave it alone; you don't need to improve it to see it.
cells.sheetLine: You shine because you built something worth shining from.
cells.verb: steering by a light you can't yet see by
cells.place: the long haul, where the weight is carried

cells.tense: You will be pushing the light forward into a future that hasn't been laid down yet.
cells.act: wait until you know which part matters, then begin with that part
cells.ask: Hold off on the pushing. Wait until one part clearly matters more than the rest of it, then start there and leave the remainder be.
cells.core:
When you want something real, you hold it up so bright it starts to strain. What's chasing you isn't the light — it's the bracing. You keep a future lit so hard that it glares, and the glare is more about how much you want it already settled than about what's actually growing here.

It's tiring in a way you might be calling excitement. What helps isn't to stop wanting — it's to let one thing ask for you first. Hold off until you know, without having to argue it, which part of this is load-bearing. Then put your hand there and leave the others be. Not because you don't care about them, but because nothing you're holding up is growing while you shout it forward.
cells.sheetLine: The feeling isn't the light. It's the strain of holding it up.
cells.verb: steering by a light you can't yet see by
cells.place: the long haul, where the weight is carried

cells.tense: You pointed yourself at something real, and you're still standing at the door after the light went.
cells.act: tend it small and ask nothing of it
cells.ask: Find one small piece of it that nobody would notice, and give that piece its due today. Hand it no job and no deadline.
cells.core:
You aimed at something real, and the aiming wore you down before the thing arrived. That's how it goes from where you stand — not giving up, just going quiet. The hope got used up against something that kept not happening, and the strength that would carry you if it did come back is spent.

What remains isn't nothing. Whatever the real thing was, a small version of it is still alive near you — smaller than the whole vision, small enough that it wouldn't impress anyone. Look after that one. Supply what it requires today and give it no assignment. Nothing gets built by asking it to prove your hope was right. You care for it because it's there, and it grows at its own rate.
cells.sheetLine: You aimed at something real. You can hold the smallest piece of it.

cells.tense: You are already lit from somewhere, and you tell the story as though the light isn't yours.
cells.act: hold your shape under the weight
cells.ask: Keep standing in what you carry here without making it smaller. Don't shrink it to fit the room, and don't stop to explain it.
cells.core:
Others can see the light in what you're pointed at, and you'll call it luck or timing or somebody else getting there first. That's not modesty — you set down the pen so long ago you can't feel your hand on it. Same for the times you've stopped shining here: you didn't notice that either.

There's nothing to reclaim and no bill to pay. Keep standing in what you carry — whatever it is. Don't shrink it down because the room seems not to see it, and don't stop to explain where it came from. You already do this. It's the one practice that needs no learning. Do it, and notice that you did.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying it. You're also the reason it's still lit.
cells.verb: steering by a light you can't yet see by
cells.place: the long haul, where the weight is carried
